title: ACB v Thomson Medical Pte Ltd
body: The Court of Appeal considered damages following an error in an assisted reproduction procedure. The claimant gave birth to a healthy child who was not genetically related to her husband. The court rejected recovery of the ordinary costs of raising the child but recognised a distinct loss of genetic affinity. It awarded damages as a percentage of the costs of raising the child. The judgment analyses corrective justice, policy limits on damages, causation and the nature of the claimant's legally protected interest. It distinguishes physical injury from the loss arising from the disruption of reproductive plans. The court stressed that the award did not treat the child as damage and sought to avoid affronting the child's dignity. The case is relevant to medical negligence, novel loss and the limits of compensatory damages.
